seven_q.Q0_posture: This document takes a posture of structural discovery: it assumes that the relational topology of attachment theory and the divine-human relationship described in Scripture share a common structure, and it seeks to map that structure precisely.
seven_q.Q1_identity: An isomorphism record (ISO-032) that maps attachment theory (Bowlby, Ainsworth, Bartholomew) onto Christian theology of prayer and worship, identifying 10 structural correspondences.
seven_q.Q2_domain: It lives at the intersection of developmental psychology and Christian theology, with contributions from philosophy of mind (relational ontology) and information theory (internal working models as information structures).
seven_q.Q3_claim: The 2D anxiety/avoidance space of attachment styles is structurally identical to the 2D space of worship postures; the four attachment styles map precisely onto four worship postures (secure trust, anxious legalism, avoidant deism, disorganized trauma theology); and the dynamics of attachment (secure base, proximity seeking, separation protest, internal working models, earned security, attachment hierarchy) map onto theological concepts (God as refuge, prayer, lament, theology proper, sanctification, first commandment).
seven_q.Q4_support: Empirical attachment research (Strange Situation, ECR-R, AGI), scriptural evidence (Psalms, James, 1 John, Exodus), and the structural correspondence of 10 independent features; the isomorphism is testable and falsifiable in both domains.
seven_q.Q5_dependencies: Depends on attachment theory as established by Bowlby, Ainsworth, Bartholomew, and Fraley; depends on scriptural descriptions of the divine-human relationship; depends on the concept of structural isomorphism; depends on the axioms of existence (A1.1), distinction (A1.2), substrate (A2.1), and grace (BC2).
seven_q.Q6_consequences: Forces a relational model of faith that cannot be reduced to cognitive assent; predicts that attachment style correlates with theological orientation; predicts that effective pastoral care must provide corrective relational experience; predicts that spiritual abuse produces disorganized attachment to God; constrains worship models to those that engage the attachment system.
seven_q.Q7_kill: Demonstrate that the 2D anxiety/avoidance model does not capture the primary dimensions of close relationships; demonstrate that earned security occurs without corrective relational experience; demonstrate that worship postures do not distribute across a 2D anxiety/avoidance space; demonstrate zero correlation between attachment style and theological orientation; break the topology by showing a structural feature present in one domain but absent in the other.

graph_summary.one_sentence: ISO-032 establishes a structural isomorphism between attachment theory's 2D anxiety/avoidance space and Christian worship postures, mapping 10 relational dynamics (secure base, proximity seeking, separation protest, IWM, earned security, attachment hierarchy) onto theological concepts (God as refuge, prayer, lament, theology proper, sanctification, first commandment), with testable predictions in both domains.
